answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 10 px wide from row 1 to row 29, with row 0 only 8 px wide, which is just a corner trim on the outline. It is a flat, face-on signboard split into stacked vertical panels: white, teal, yellow with a '3', and grey. No row band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow. There is no ellipse, and the width never widens and narrows again. The dark rows at 7, 19 and 29 are panel dividers and outline. The top is a flat rectangle with no overhanging cap plate, so this is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim sign post with a dark top cap, a light-grey body, an orange panel carrying the number 3, and a dark base. Its measured values are 12 visible tones per tile, 13% near-flat coverage and 0% neutral dark edges. That matches kiosk-a (12 tones, 0% flat) and beats bus-shelter-a (6 tones, 9% flat), though it falls well short of vending-a (20 tones). The outline is a tinted dark blue-grey, not neutral black, so it counts as a dark material tone. The grey body has about 3-4 steps, with a highlight strip on the left and a darker right side. This is a little less than the 5-6 steps on the richer references. The 13% flat coverage comes from the plain body and base sections, which are a mild flat-fill concern but fairly small. This is a thin, sparse object, so I judged density mainly by eye. It sits at the level of the shipped modern_city props like bus-shelter-a and kiosk-a, and a careful artist would accept it next to them without it looking sticker-like. Its shading is somewhat simpler than vending-a.

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 10px wide from row 1 to row 29, with only row 0 narrower at 8px (a corner-trimmed outline). It is a stack of flat, face-on rectangular panels (white sign, teal header, yellow '3' panel, grey base) separated by dark 1-row outlines at rows 7, 19 and 29. There is no ellipse cap that widens and narrows, no front-edge line with eave shadow, and no horizontal surface visible from above. The top white panel (rows 1-6) is a vertical face with a light-to-dark shading split, not a cap plate. The cap does not overhang the shaft, so this matches the red 'column: flat band cap' reference rather than the green ellipse cap.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim pole sign with a light-grey top, an orange panel carrying a '3' and a dark base. Measured facts: 12 visible tones per tile (kiosk-a 12, bus-shelter-a 6, vending-a 20), 13% near-flat coverage (bus-shelter 9%, kiosk and vending 0%), and 0% neutral dark edges, so the outline is tinted rather than near-black. Judged by eye, the body is a thin sign with about 3-4 steps per material (pole grey, orange panel, dark edge) and a small 'sticker-like' number plate, shallower than the kiosk and vending machine, which have 5-6 steps and detailed panels. It is at least as dense as the bus shelter, and as a thin prop it is judged by eye rather than on the numbers. The slightly higher flat coverage and fewer shading steps on the pole body leave it a little thinner than the best references, though it is acceptable next to the bus shelter. When in doubt, fail.
